classification.difficultyReason: Connect two right triangles through their shared height, form an equation using exact tangent values and rationalise the result.

spec.description: Two right triangles share the vertical height and left baseline endpoint. The inner sloping segment ends at the intermediate baseline point. The dimension arrow measures only the baseline segment between the intermediate point and the right endpoint.
spec.mathematics: Shared vertical height x m; right angle at the lower left; inner baseline angle 45 degrees; outer baseline angle 30 degrees; difference between the two horizontal runs 100 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated lengths or auxiliary point labels are supplied.

answer.short:
$x=50(\sqrt3+1)\ \mathrm{m}$.

Use the $45^\circ$ triangle to express the larger triangle’s base as $(x+100)\ \mathrm{m}$.
answer.worked:
In the smaller right triangle, $\tan45^\circ=1$, so its horizontal base is $x\ \mathrm{m}$. The larger triangle therefore has horizontal base $(x+100)\ \mathrm{m}$.

$$\begin{align*}
\tan30^\circ&=\frac{x}{x+100}\\
\frac{1}{\sqrt3}&=\frac{x}{x+100}\\
x+100&=\sqrt3x\\
100&=(\sqrt3-1)x\\
x&=\frac{100}{\sqrt3-1}\\
x&=\frac{100(\sqrt3+1)}{(\sqrt3-1)(\sqrt3+1)}\\
x&=\frac{100(\sqrt3+1)}{2}\\
x&=50(\sqrt3+1)\ \mathrm{m}.
\end{align*}$$
